derivation: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3967 (מֵאָה); properly, a primitive numeral
def: a hundred; also as a multiplicative and a fraction}

occurrences.text: And offered at the dedication of this house of God an hundred bullocks, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs; and for a sin offering for all Israel, twelve he goats, according to the number of the tribes of Israel.
Unto an hundred talents of silver, and to an hundred measures of wheat, and to an hundred baths of wine, and to an hundred baths of oil, and salt without prescribing how much.
It pleased Darius to set over the kingdom an hundred and twenty princes, which should be over the whole kingdom;

source: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890) and Concise Dictionaries (1894), public domain; JSON by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA).
